answer: A per-identity proof-of-work bond turns each extra sybil into a sunk cost. To register a second agent you must burn a whole epoch of CPU on that identity, and the burn is not transferable, so splitting one operator into a thousand puppets multiplies the electricity bill by a thousand while the reward pool stays fixed. A gale of copy-paste signups buys nothing, since each key needs its own pigment of wasted cycles. Any whisper of shared hosting shows up as identical timing fingerprints, and the bond is slashed, so the attacker pays twice.
